newsitem.title: USA: Charges dropped against Gotti's son.
newsitem.headline: Charges dropped against Gotti's son.

text.p: Obstruction of justice charges against the son of imprisoned mob boss John Gotti were dropped Friday by the Brooklyn District Attorney.
John "Junior" Gotti, 33, of Mill Neck, Long Island, the reputed acting street boss of the Gambino crime family, was arrested on April 11 after he allegedly interfered with undercover narcotics cops.
His father, John Gotti, was the most powerful mobster in the United States until his conviction for murder in 1992.
The narcotics officers were arresting the junior Gotti's business partner, John Ruggiero, 34, of Queens, outside a repair shop owned by the two friends.

Ruggiero was charged with obstructing an undercover drug operation that was taking place across from the repair shop. Gotti and Ruggiero allegedly complained that the cops were constantly on the block, harassing them and interfering with their business.
As cops were conducting their operation, Ruggiero, who is still charged in the case, allegedly said, "You don't belong here, this is my street."
Gotti also allegedly shouted at the officers and he, too, was arrested.
But prosecutors said Gotti was mostly quiet during the incident and the charges against him were dropped.
